title: Solar Panel Size for 2000 Sq Ft Home: A Guide for American Homeowners
excerpt: Find the ideal solar panel size for a 2000 sq ft home with this comprehensive guide
content:
Solar Panel Size Calculator

To determine the solar panel size needed for a 2000 sq ft home, consider factors like electricity usage, roof space, and local solar radiation. A general rule of thumb is to install 1-2 watts of solar panel power per square foot of living space.

Calculating Solar Panel Size

Assuming an average electricity usage of 30-40 kWh per day, a 2000 sq ft home would require a solar panel system between 5-8 kilowatts (kW). To calculate the number of solar panels, divide the total kW by the wattage of each panel (approximately 300-400 watts).

Roof Space and Orientation

Consider the available roof space and orientation for optimal solar panel placement. South-facing roofs receive the most direct sunlight, while east- and west-facing roofs receive less radiation. Ensure at least 3 square feet of unobstructed roof space per kilowatt of solar panel power.

Conclusion

Visit SolarAtlas to find solar data for your city and determine the ideal solar panel size for your 2000 sq ft home. Consult with a professional solar installer to ensure a custom-fit solar panel system that meets your energy needs and budget.
